body:
Codex review: this still needs some work.

**Summary**
This issue establishes an unresolved ACP workflow defect: the agent can wait for a human answer that the bridge cannot collect. Current main and the latest release retain the missing relay; related channel repairs do not resolve this boundary.

Reproducibility: yes. source establishes the path: trigger ask_user in an acp-bridge session and observe tool activity without a question-answer relay. The historical release trace supports this mechanism, but no current-main runtime reproduction was executed.

**Maintainer decision needed**
- **Question:** Should ACP clients without a question-answer contract receive immediate no-answer behavior, or should the bridge gain a structured interactive question relay?
- **Recommendation:** **Prevent unsupported waits:** Treat question support as connection-scoped and return a visible no-answer outcome when the attached client cannot answer.
- **Why:** The documented ACP bridge supports exec permission requests, while ask_user requires free text, multiple questions, and multiple selections; no recorded decision establishes how ACP clients should answer these.

**Next step**
Choose the ACP question capability contract before dispatching repair, then require real stdio-client proof with an isolated Gateway.


<details>
<summary>Review details</summary>

Best possible solution:

Use connection-scoped question support to avoid unanswerable waits with a visible explanation, and add interactive relay only through an explicit question-answer contract.

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue?

Yes, source establishes the path: trigger ask_user in an acp-bridge session and observe tool activity without a question-answer relay. The historical release trace supports this mechanism, but no current-main runtime reproduction was executed.

Is this the best way to solve the issue?

Unclear for the suggested permission relay: its authorization choices do not preserve the full question contract. Preventing unsupported waits through connection-scoped capability handling is the narrower immediate direction.

AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant.

Remaining risk / open question:

- No current-main runtime run establishes the exact wait duration or expiry-to-next-turn recovery.
- Reusing permission approval choices for ordinary questions could produce unintended answers from clients configured to approve permissions automatically.

Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [725da12cc31c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/725da12cc31cbb923ca9884beddb316e3ca4ac32).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Label changes</summary>

Label changes:

No label changes.

Label justifications:

- `P1`: A reported ACP editor or harness turn blocks on an unavailable human interaction, and current source retains the failure path.
- `impact:session-state`: The pending question holds the active agent turn until an answer elsewhere, cancellation, or timeout.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Evidence reviewed</summary>

What I checked:

- **Current-main comparison:** The reviewed checkout is 8c22de3f1d06a878de0eb5c0531457584d874e82. GitHub main is 725da12cc31cbb923ca9884beddb316e3ca4ac32; the intervening change touches only updater custody code, tests, and updating documentation. The reviewed ACP and question paths are unchanged, and the working tree is clean. ([725da12cc31c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/725da12cc31cbb923ca9884beddb316e3ca4ac32))
- **Question events have no bridge handler:** Gateway event dispatch handles chat, exec.approval.requested, and agent events. The agent-event translator handles approval and tool streams, emitting in_progress tool activity with raw input but no question-answer operation. Searches across src/acp and packages/acp-core found no ask_user or question RPC relay. ([`src/acp/translator.prompt-stream.ts:139`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8c22de3f1d06a878de0eb5c0531457584d874e82/src/acp/translator.prompt-stream.ts#L139), [8c22de3f1d06](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8c22de3f1d06a878de0eb5c0531457584d874e82))
- **Bridge sessions can receive the blocking tool:** Primary-session registration gates ask_user using isPrimaryBootstrapRun and tool-deny policy. That classifier excludes subagent: and acp: worker sessions, whereas default bridge sessions use acp-bridge:. No connected-client question capability is checked. ([`src/agents/openclaw-tools.registration.ts:134`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8c22de3f1d06a878de0eb5c0531457584d874e82/src/agents/openclaw-tools.registration.ts#L134), [8c22de3f1d06](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8c22de3f1d06a878de0eb5c0531457584d874e82))
- **Text delivery does not supply an alternative answer flow:** The embedded subscriber sends question prompts through onToolResult. Gateway webchat delivery retains tool replies only when they contain media, so a text-only question does not become an ordinary chat reply through this path. ([`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-reply-dispatch.ts:553`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8c22de3f1d06a878de0eb5c0531457584d874e82/src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-reply-dispatch.ts#L553), [8c22de3f1d06](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8c22de3f1d06a878de0eb5c0531457584d874e82))
- **Question lifecycle and documented limits:** ask_user registers question.request and awaits question.waitAnswer. Its default human timeout is 900 seconds, subject to earlier run cancellation or the overall run budget. The documented answer surfaces include Control UI, TUI, native apps, and channels, without an ACP answer contract: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/ask-user. ([`src/agents/tools/ask-user-tool.ts:564`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8c22de3f1d06a878de0eb5c0531457584d874e82/src/agents/tools/ask-user-tool.ts#L564), [8c22de3f1d06](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8c22de3f1d06a878de0eb5c0531457584d874e82))
- **Latest release retains the missing handler:** GitHub identifies v2026.9.9 as the latest release. Reading its ACP prompt-stream source confirms the same chat, exec approval, and agent dispatch without a question-event branch. ([`src/acp/translator.prompt-stream.ts:171`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bcfc88812a35243893585dbeca87ca41b48272ca/src/acp/translator.prompt-stream.ts#L171), [bcfc88812a35](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bcfc88812a35243893585dbeca87ca41b48272ca))

</details>

<details>
<summary>How this review workflow works</summary>

- ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR.
- Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments.
- A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch.
- PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only.
- Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only.
- Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge.
- Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`.
- Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation.

</details>
